scope: City of Pittsburgh, 2020 census tracts whose land is mostly inside the city limits
notes: Single source of truth for scoring, read by src/visionpitts/scoring.py, src/visionpitts/factors.py and app/src/lib/scoring.ts. Factor values are OBSERVED DATA computed in Python: seven are 0-1 percentile ranks across the ranked City of Pittsburgh tracts, and subsidy eligibility is a grade of 0, 0.5 or 1 (not a percentile). factor_options are the switches for how the observed factors are built. The fit matrix, weights and presets are VALUE JUDGMENTS and are labeled as such everywhere they appear; every cell changed in v0.4.0 is logged in fit.changes. After any change here, rerun scripts 02, 03, 04 and scripts/make_parity_fixture.py.

factors.label: Affordability need
factors.description: Renter households at or below 50% of area median income (HUD CHAS, HAMFI). Count, ranked across city tracts.

factors.label: Market strength
factors.description: Reinvestment Fund Market Value Analysis category in 2021 (80%) plus the direction of change since 2016 (20%).
factors.direction_note: Higher = stronger or rising housing market

factors.label: Displacement risk
factors.description: Composite of CDC Social Vulnerability Index (0.3), CHAS cost burden among renters ≤50% AMI (0.3), eviction filing rate (0.2) and vouchers per renter household (0.2). Each part is percentile-ranked; weights renormalize over the parts a tract has.
factors.direction_note: Higher = more residents vulnerable to displacement

factors.label: Subsidy eligibility
factors.description: 1.0 if a LIHTC Qualified Census Tract or in a Small-Area DDA (2026). 0.5 if the only designation is an Opportunity Zone or CDBG area (2018, carried from 2010 geography). 0 if none.

factors.label: Transit access
factors.description: Weekday PRT departures at stops within 400 m, per household (ACS 2020–24). Tracts under 400 households are divided by 400.
factors.direction_note: Higher = more frequent nearby transit per household

factors.label: Flood exposure
factors.description: Share of tract land inside a HAND-derived inundation footprint (screening model, not FEMA).
factors.direction_note: Higher = more land exposed to flooding. A terrain model, medium confidence at best.

factors.label: Residents 65 and over
factors.description: Share of residents aged 65 or older (ACS B01001). Tracts with existing senior buildings read high.
factors.direction_note: Higher = a larger share of residents are 65 or older

factors.label: 2–4 unit homes
factors.description: Share of housing units in 2–4 unit buildings (ACS B25024). A built-form signal, not zoning.
factors.direction_note: Higher = more of the housing stock is in 2–4 unit buildings

fit.label: VALUE JUDGMENT. How much each typology benefits from a high value of each factor (+) or from a low value (−). Magnitude 0–1; 0 = the factor says nothing about this typology. Editable; recorded in docs/assumptions.md. Cells changed in v0.4.0 are listed in `changes`.

scoring.formula: S(t,k) = sum_f w_f * c(x_tf, d_kf) / sum_f w_f * |d_kf|, over factors with data and w_f > 0. c = d*x if d >= 0 else |d|*(1-x). Dividing by |d| makes S a weighted-average fit in [0,1] so typologies with larger fit totals are not favored.

presets.label: Anti-displacement
presets.blurb: Protect vulnerable renters first; market strength matters less.

presets.label: Market-led
presets.blurb: Go where unsubsidized construction can work.

presets.label: Transit-first
presets.blurb: Put homes where the buses already run.

presets.label: Climate-resilient
presets.blurb: Keep homes out of flood zones and near frequent transit; favor attached and multi-unit forms.

confidence.rule: Start from data age vs 2026: <=2 yrs high, 3-5 medium, >5 low. Downgrade one level (never below low) for: coverage < 90%, dominant 2010->2020 crosswalk share < 0.8, CV > 30% (or, for the two ACS share factors, a CV that cannot be computed because the estimate is zero), or an imputed/missing component. Transit: down when the household count is floored at 400 or its CV > 30%. Displacement (R-5): down only if fewer than 3 of the 4 parts are present, the burden CV > 30%, or the eviction estimate draws on several ZIP codes and none holds at least 80% of the tract's housing units. Flood: medium at best because it is a terrain model, low where more than 50% of the land reads as inundated. Subsidy: high for a 2026 designation or none, medium when the only designation is from 2018, low when that also crossed a large 2010->2020 boundary change.

pressure.label: OBSERVED, derived. market_pressure = queen-contiguity spatial lag of market_strength minus own market_strength. Positive = neighbors are stronger. Not a scoring factor; drives the market-pressure map mode and the watch list.
pressure.bivariate: need tercile (L/M/H) x market change direction (falling/flat/rising from MVA 2016->2021); watch list = H-rising.

bins.note: Fixed choropleth breaks for 0-1 scores, identical across scenarios so colors compare.
